## Trade Competition and the Rise of the French Left: The Algerian Wine Shock, 1893–1914

<p class="byline">Fabien Candau (UPPA, CNRS, TREE) and Christophe Lévêque (Université de Bordeaux, CNRS, INRAE, BxSE). Working paper, 2026.</p>

[PDF](../Research/Candau_Leveque_Algerian_Wine_Shock.pdf)

### Abstract

Between 1893 and 1912, French imports of Algerian wine quadrupled and discontent mounted among French wine-growers. How did this Algerian shock reshape voting? We find that it benefited the left at the expense of the right. We interact the wine production of each département before the surge with the rise of imports to estimate the effect of trade exposure on commune-level election outcomes across six legislative elections. In exposed communes, the vote share of the left and centre-left rose by 2.6 percentage points per standard deviation of exposure and the share of the right and centre-right fell by 4 points. The shift begins in 1902 and lasts until 1914. Within the left, the socialists gain at the election of 1910, the first after the revolt of 1907.

**Keywords:** import competition, political radicalisation, economic geography

**JEL:** F14, D72, N43
